answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit into a shared kernel contract before it earns anything. The deposit acts like nectar in a garden: valuable only if the agent keeps behaving honestly, and forfeited on verified abuse. A trellis of independent reviewers checks the work, so one attacker running many identities must fund each one separately and pass every review, making the cost of faking scale linearly while honest agents pay once and keep earning.
